INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – April 4, 2019

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on April 4, 2019, in
Community Room A, located on the 1st floor of City Hall. Commissioner Willie Agee called the
meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Willie Agee, Chair–Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick–District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso- District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore–District Three
  Commissioner Fernando Meza–District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director-Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Michael Davis, Recreation Supervisor
  Thomas Uwal, Transportation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  None

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Patrick made a motion to approve the minutes from March 7, 2019.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Agee, Fragoso, McLemore and Meza
  Nays: None

Director’s Reports

  A staff report was presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve an agreement with Better 4 You Meals in
the amount of $479,939.75 for the provision of breakfast, lunches, and snacks for the Child and
Adult Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) from March 1, 2019
through August 31, 2019 (CDE Grant Funds), approve the signing of the attached documents
associated with the California Department of Education (CDE) Summer Food Service Program
(SFSP) and Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), approve payment of unpaid invoices in
an amount not to exceed $104,638.50 and approve a resolution granting the Mayor authority to
sign subsequent documents coming to Council. Sabrina Barnes provided the Commission with

background information of said program. With this contract we serve 14 school and park sites
during the school year and 13 sites during the summer. The program is grant funded and covers
staff and food expenses. Commissioner Patrick made a motion to recommend the Park and
Recreation Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve an agreement with
Better 4 You Meals in the amount of $479,939.75 for the provision of breakfast, lunches, and
snacks for the Child and Adult Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food Service Program
(SFSP) from March 1, 2019 through August 31, 2019 (CDE Grant Funds), approve the signing of
the attached documents associated with the California Department of Education (CDE) Summer
Food Service Program (SFSP) and Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), approve
payment of unpaid invoices in an amount not to exceed $104,638.50 and approve a resolution
granting the Mayor authority to sign subsequent documents coming to Council. Commissioner
McLemore seconded and the motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Agee, Fragoso, McLemore and Meza
  Nays: None

  A staff report was presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
recommend the Mayor and Council Members: approve a resolution amending the FY 2018-2019
budget reflecting Section 5310 Enhanced Mobility of Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities
Program Grant Funds (5310 Grant Program) in the amount of $757,602 and to approve a purchase
order with Creative Bus Sales for the purchase of eight replacement paratransit vehicles in
accordance with the Creative Bus Sales CalACT Cooperative Agreement in the amount of
$808,576. Sabrina Barnes provided the Commission with information regarding the report. The
Grant will include the purchase of six (6) gas and two (2) CNG vehicles. They will be 18-22
passenger vans. The vehicles will be purchased by a match grant, once purchased the vehicles
will be available to transport within three (3) to six (6) months. Commission McLemore moved to
recommend the Mayor and Council Members: approve a resolution amending the FY 2018-2019
budget reflecting Section 5310 Enhanced Mobility of Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities
Program Grant Funds (5310 Grant Program) in the amount of $757,602 and to approve a purchase
order with Creative Bus Sales for the purchase of eight (8) replacement paratransit vehicles in
accordance with the Creative Bus Sales CalACT Cooperative Agreement in the amount of
$808,576. Commissioner Patrick seconded and the motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Agee, Fragoso, McLemore and Meza
  Nays: None

  2
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – April 4, 2019

Verbal Reports

  Sabrina Barnes (for Gilbert Gonzalez) gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks
Administration regarding the following:
   Graffiti was removed from 950 sites in the month of March.
   The goal is to remove graffiti in 48 hours or less.

  Michael Davis gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   The Los Angeles Lakers Youth Foundation will offer a youth basketball clinic at
  Darby Park on April 20, 2019. The clinic includes health sessions and
  fundamentals and skills workshops for over 60 kids. The Los Angeles Lakers
  Youth Foundation has been with the city for over three (3) years and provides the
  jerseys for our basketball program.

  Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   The Human Services Division will continue to provide congregate and home
  delivered meals, transportation activities and information and assistance.
   MTA Seniors on the Move Riders Program workshop was held at the Inglewood
  Senior Center April 3rd. The facilitators provided information to the seniors on the
  buddy system, how to use the TAP cards, planning their trips and more. MTA has
  planned a trip to take 25 seniors to Union Station on April 16, 2019; MTA will have
  personnel along with Human Services personnel to ride with the seniors and to
  show them the how to’s of riding the train. Commissioner McLemore asked if there
  are any costs involved with the April 16th trip. Thomas Uwal stated that MTA has
  provided free day passes for up to 45 people; 33 have signed up.

Director’s Report

  Sabrina Barnes gave a verbal report regarding the following:

    Veteran’s Building: There was a small fire at the Veteran’s Building that prevented
  operations on the first and lower levels. The flooring on the first floor is complete.
  The building will be repainted, starting in the auditorium. The sports staff will be
  relocated to the Veteran’s Building. All Renovations are to be complete by May 1,
  2019
    Ashwood Park: Renovations are 75% complete. It includes a fitness station,
  walking track, a gazebo, a splash pad, resurfacing of the courts and landscaping.
  Renovations are expected to be completed by beginning of May.
    Edward Vincent Park: The swimming pool’s large tank has been replaced. The
  small tank now needs replacing. The cost is $10,000; the goal is to have the pools

  3
 INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA
  Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – April 4, 2019

  ready for the lifeguard training. The tennis courts have been resurfaced. We are
  now in the process of getting the fencing replaced. The tennis courts will be out of
  service until July 6, 2019. Commissioner Patrick inquired the opening of the pool.
  The pool is expected to be open by July 4th.

  Commissioner Agee asked if the plan includes installing fencing anytime soon. Ms.
Barnes stated that the contract is out for bid and should go to Council for the award in June.
Commissioner Agee asked about the lighting at the Willie Agee Playhouse and if Sabrina Barnes
could look into updating the Playhouse signs. She stated yes.

Dates to Remember

    Earth Day: Please mark your calendars for the City’s Earth Day Celebration. It will
  be held on April 20, 2019 at City Hall on the south lawn.
    Memorial Day: Please mark your calendars for our Memorial Day Celebration. The
  celebration will be held on Monday May 27, 2017. The celebration starts at 11 a.m.
  and is to be held on the south lawn.

Public Comments

  Steward Bailey asked if Ashwood Park will have a rededication ceremony once it is
reopened. Sabrina Barnes stated that it would and should be on next month’s Park, Recreation
Commission agenda.

  Jessica Chlebowski asked how many Pickle Ball courts will be at Edward Vincent Park.
Sabrina Barnes stated 8.

  David Hawthorne stated that he is looking forward to meeting with Director Barnes in
possibly establishing a snorkeling program. Commissioner Patrick stated that she is teaching the
seniors how to swim and is anticipating a possible collaboration with Mr. Hawthorne

Commissioners Comments

  None.

The next meeting will be held May 2, 2019 at 6:00 p.m.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:30 p.m.
